messages:
maria: Quick spike — running a fairness probe focused on KV-cache hit skew across tenants. Observed some tenants with ~35% lower throughput despite same qps. Starting a thread to coordinate tests.
kevin: Can you share the harness config you used? replay or synth?
maria: Replay harness — replayed traces from last week's prod window. Config below:
```json
{"mode":"replay","trace":"2026-03-10-prod-window","scale":0.8,"preserve_ts":true}
```
liam: Did you control for kernel selection? different kernels can change latency vs batch tradeoffs.
maria: Yes — ran with kernel_v1 and kernel_v2. kernel_v2 had better avg throughput but worse tail for small tenants.
anya: Do we have KV cache hit-rate per-tenant? If cache miss pattern differs it will change latency a lot.
maria: Per-tenant KV hit rates we pulled: tenant_A 0.92, tenant_B 0.61, tenant_C 0.88. Tenant_B correlates with higher p99.
kevin: Suggest an apples-to-apples run: same arrival seed, same sequence length distribution, pin batching params (`batch_cap`, `max_delay`), and toggle only kernel.
liam: Agreed. Also set `continuous_batching.enabled=false` for baseline so we can measure the scheduler's effect in isolation.
bench-bot: automated-run 1823456799 started: cmd `./bench --replay --trace 2026-03-10-prod-window --scale 0.8` ETA 12m
maria: After kernel flip: kernel_v1 p99=210ms, kernel_v2 p99=380ms for tenant_B. throughput down ~18% for B.
anya: Interesting — kernel_v2 changes service ordering enough to affect KV cache eviction timing, could cause more cache churn for low-locality tenants.
kevin: Let's run a synthetic mix with controlled KV locality to verify. Use synthetic generator with tenant affinity and fixed seeds to remove trace noise.
maria: Synth config (short):
```yaml
mode: synth
tenants:
  - id: A
    locality: high
  - id: B
    locality: low
batch_cap: 64
max_delay_ms: 8
seed: 1337
```
liam: One more metric: compute fairness = p99_ratio = max(p99)/median(p99) across tenants. We saw p99_ratio ~2.1 under kernel_v2, ~1.1 under kernel_v1.
maria: TL;DR: kernel_v2 improves avg throughput but amplifies KV-miss-sensitive tail for low-locality tenants. Root cause hypothesis: kernel_v2's scheduling increases multi-tenant interleaving that causes earlier evictions in the KV cache for some tenants.
kevin: Mitigations to test: 1) tighten `max_delay` to 4ms 2) reduce `batch_cap` for small/low-locality tenants via tenant-aware batching 3) fallback to kernel_v1 for flagged tenants until kernel_v2 fixes the eviction pattern.
maria: Also added NVTX + perf counters in the next run to capture per-request KV miss spans and GC-like eviction spikes. Will post traces.
kevin: I'll open a perf PR with telemetry hooks and a canary that pins kernel per-tenant. Also adding a synthetic test case to the apples-to-apples matrix.
maria: Anyone want to own rollback plan if canary degrades prod? @liam?
liam: I'll own rollback plan and the emergency canary cutoff (p99 spike > 1.5x baseline). :thumbsup:
bench-bot: run complete: summary: kernel_v1 p99_median=220ms kernel_v2 p99_median=300ms overall_throughput_delta=-6%, tenant_B_throughput=-18%, p99_ratio_kernel_v1=1.08 p99_ratio_kernel_v2=2.13
maria: Ok closing loop — next steps: 1) kevin PR + telemetry 2) synthetic confirm with controlled KV patterns 3) update canary policy to pin kernel per-tenant and monitor p99_ratio. Filing a follow-up doc for rollout notes.
